notes: ACH debit authorization route (owner 2026-11-19: Condition One's "Sign & Authorize ACH" failed with writes_disabled; owner chose "Go with A", a server write path). The Settings bank account card (AchAuthorizationForm.tsx) inserted and updated public.ach_authorizations from the browser; the AWS client refuses every table outside AWS_WRITE_TABLES with writes_disabled before any request, the generic /data/write route refuses the table, and SQL 136 accepts its writes only on a server write path. ach-authorization.mjs (new) adds the route save-ach-authorization: a member of the tenant (resolveTenantAccess canConfigure), the tenant's own stakeholder_accounts row, action get, authorize or revoke. The server writes authorized_name and form_text from the stored account (custname; last four from chk_acct, else provider_last_four, else "on file"), authorized_by from the verified sign-in, ip_address and user_agent from API Gateway; request fields are ignored. authorize returns an existing active row instead of inserting; revoke sets is_active false, revoked_at, revoked_by and revoke_reason on the active row. Each write sets request.money_write immediately before it runs (money-write-flag.mjs). Nothing is debited and no provider is called. app-services.mjs registers the route (Class A) and dispatches it; it imports the new module statically, so ach-authorization.mjs is ADDed first, just before app-services.mjs in order. app-services.mjs live_sha256 is main's accepted transfer to bank bytes, put live in production by the seventh full rebuild (lambda-rebuild-plan.json production history 6, apply 43464046767) and unchanged since; a read-only production overlay inspect must confirm them before any apply. No SQL change. No release-lock change. The website change that calls the route is a separate PR.
